checked_and_sound: Refresher pattern, twelve screens: recall (Zs at the far end through Ze, the submain and the circuit, with the two slips) and Refresh the why / Skip to the practice (screen 6); what it is for with the checklist and the red consequence; the why with its interactive (length slider and light/heavy load, two stacked bars against 6.90 V and 3.64 Ω, a still at 4.89 A and 45.0 m); a judgement check on a three-phase drop joining a single-phase circuit; the worked submain line by line; Section A 3(g) to 3(j) each with the scenario, carried parts and a typed answer with three named slips; Section B on every length of the run (five points, any three); one changed-numbers item (the longest run meeting both limits); Keep this.

The causal step is shown: each metre adds mV/A/m × I to the drop but a fixed 30.976 mΩ to the loop whatever the load, so Zs binds for a light load (near 104.5 m) and the drop for a heavy one (near 38.9 m); the Zs bar does not move when the load changes.
The worked example is the showroom submain, not a slide example: his slides have no end-to-end example, and lessons 1 to 7 already used theirs.
The why uses a board chosen for the picture (0.40 Ω, 1.00 V) so it does not give away 3(g) and 3(h); the check and changed-numbers item use new numbers.
Lesson 4's promise kept: It ≥ In ÷ (Ca × Cg × Ci × 0.86) = 11.63 A for the submain.
Contested points taught as contested, simply: which end sets the thermal check (both ends worked, 0.50 and 1.43 mm²); the phase-by-phase route for an unbalanced submain (1.97 V).
Practice values said simply where used: the 1.5 m vertical runs, the 4 mm² SWA and 10 A type C, the 6 A type C, k 46, the 20% third harmonic, Ca 1.00, 6 kA breakers.
No source talk in the words; Section B points and the card's traps keep their cites as data only.
